title: heif-dec and heif-info can release an uninitialized URI pointer
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not specified for this finding)
summary: For a urim sample entry without a URI box, heif-dec -S and heif-info could print and release an uninitialized pointer, depending on build causing a crash or access to a URI from a previous track. The library itself is not affected; the issue is in the two helper tools.
ai_role: The item-level libheif advisory explicitly attributes discovery to Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-QVQYWGC7. The release notes independently state that all listed security issues were found by the scanner. The Anthropic program sources establish model-based scanning, but no per-case model is identified.
classification_note: The primary advisory establishes a publicly disclosed security finding and direct Anthropic OSS Scanner attribution. No CVE had been assigned in the libheif release notes at the checked time; the distinct GHSA is used. No exploitation or zero-day status is asserted.
remediation_note: Both tools now use/release the URI only on successful lookup, and the API initializes its output pointer to null. Fixed in libheif 1.23.7. The libheif v1.23.7 security release is dated 2026-10-26; deployed patch status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: A crafted urim track without a URI makes heif-dec -S or heif-info process an uninitialized pointer and crash before frame decoding; use-after-free/double-free details do not establish code execution.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.
